subcategory_title: Organizational mission is understood and informs cybersecurity risk management
subcategory_outcome: The mission of the organization is articulated and used as the lens through which cybersecurity risks are evaluated.
implementation_guidance: Document the organization's mission statement and key business objectives in a place every cybersecurity decision references. When approving a control, defending an exception, or sizing a residual risk, ask whether the choice supports or undermines the mission. Brief incoming security staff on mission context within their first week.
evidence_artifacts: Mission statement, cybersecurity charter linking back to mission, sample risk decisions citing mission impact.

subcategory_title: Internal and external stakeholders are understood, and their needs and expectations regarding cybersecurity risk management are understood and considered
subcategory_outcome: Stakeholders are mapped and their cybersecurity expectations are explicit inputs to the program.
implementation_guidance: Build a stakeholder register: internal (board, exec, IT, business units, audit), external (regulators, customers, suppliers, insurers, communities). Capture each one's cybersecurity-relevant expectations. Update at least annually and whenever a major contract or regulatory change occurs.
evidence_artifacts: Stakeholder register, customer security questionnaire responses, regulator correspondence log.

subcategory_title: Legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements regarding cybersecurity—including privacy and civil liberties obligations—are understood and managed
subcategory_outcome: All applicable laws, regulations, and contract clauses are tracked and traced to controls.
implementation_guidance: Maintain a regulatory inventory keyed to the jurisdictions you operate in (KSA NCA ECC, PDPL, GDPR if EU presence, sector-specific rules). Map each requirement to the control(s) that satisfy it. Flag changes via legal-update subscriptions.
evidence_artifacts: Regulatory inventory, requirement-to-control mapping matrix, legal-update review minutes.

subcategory_title: Critical objectives, capabilities, and services that external stakeholders depend on or expect from the organization are understood and communicated
subcategory_outcome: The services on which others depend are inventoried and protected accordingly.
implementation_guidance: Identify which products/services external parties rely on. Categorize by impact (revenue, reputation, public safety) if disrupted. Communicate dependencies to suppliers and customers via SLAs and onboarding materials.
evidence_artifacts: Critical service inventory, business impact analysis (BIA), customer-facing SLA documents.

subcategory_title: Outcomes, capabilities, and services that the organization depends on are understood and communicated
subcategory_outcome: The supplier ecosystem and external dependencies are mapped and risk-tiered.
implementation_guidance: Inventory all third-party services that could halt operations (cloud, comms, payments, key software). Tier by criticality and concentration risk. Establish escalation paths for dependency failures.
evidence_artifacts: Third-party dependency map, criticality tiering, runbook for dependency failure.

subcategory_title: Risk management objectives are established and agreed to by organizational stakeholders
subcategory_outcome: Cybersecurity risk objectives are explicit, written, and signed off by leadership.
implementation_guidance: Define what 'good' looks like for cyber risk: objectives such as 'no critical findings open >30 days', 'phishing fail rate <5%', 'audit findings closed within target dates'. Get formal sign-off from the board or risk committee.
evidence_artifacts: Cybersecurity risk objectives document, board minutes approving objectives.

subcategory_title: Risk appetite and risk tolerance statements are established, communicated, and maintained
subcategory_outcome: How much risk the organization is willing to bear is documented per category.
implementation_guidance: Develop appetite statements per risk category (Strategic / Operational / Financial / Cyber / Privacy / Compliance). Express tolerance in measurable terms: e.g. 'We accept up to 2 High operational risks; zero High compliance risks.' Review annually.
evidence_artifacts: Risk appetite statement, risk tolerance thresholds per category, annual review record.

subcategory_title: Cybersecurity risk management activities and outcomes are included in enterprise risk management processes
subcategory_outcome: Cyber risk is integrated with enterprise risk, not siloed.
implementation_guidance: Cyber risks appear in the enterprise risk register, not just a separate cyber-only register. Cyber-risk reviews use the same likelihood/impact scoring as other enterprise risks. Cyber-risk reports go to the same forum (Audit Committee, ERM Committee).
evidence_artifacts: Enterprise risk register including cyber rows, cross-functional risk-review meeting minutes.

subcategory_title: Strategic direction that describes appropriate risk response options is established and communicated
subcategory_outcome: Standard risk-response playbook (mitigate / transfer / avoid / accept) is documented.
implementation_guidance: Publish a risk-response framework explaining when each option applies. Tie to financial thresholds (e.g. accept losses below $X without escalation, mitigate above). Train risk owners on the framework.
evidence_artifacts: Risk response framework document, training records, sample risk treatment decisions citing the framework.

subcategory_title: Lines of communication across the organization are established for cybersecurity risks, including risks from suppliers and other third parties
subcategory_outcome: Risk information flows up, down, and across without bottlenecks.
implementation_guidance: Define escalation paths: who tells whom about which risks, in what timeframe. Include cross-organization paths (subsidiary → parent, business unit → security). Test the paths with quarterly drills.
evidence_artifacts: Risk communication chart, escalation runbook, drill records.

subcategory_title: A standardized method for calculating, documenting, categorizing, and prioritizing cybersecurity risks is established and communicated
subcategory_outcome: Risks are scored consistently using a documented method.
implementation_guidance: Adopt a single risk-scoring methodology (likelihood × impact, or FAIR for quantitative shops). Train all risk owners. Document the rubric (what makes likelihood 'High' vs 'Medium'). Calibrate quarterly to prevent score drift.
evidence_artifacts: Risk scoring methodology document, calibration session records, risk register entries demonstrating consistent scoring.

subcategory_title: Strategic opportunities are characterized and are included in organizational cybersecurity risk discussions
subcategory_outcome: Cyber risk discussions also surface opportunities, not just threats.
implementation_guidance: When evaluating risks, also identify opportunities (faster customer onboarding via stronger identity, market access via certifications, premium pricing for security-as-differentiator). Track opportunities alongside threats.
evidence_artifacts: Risk register including opportunity entries, business case docs citing security-driven opportunities.

subcategory_title: Organizational leadership is responsible and accountable for cybersecurity risk and fosters a culture that is risk-aware, ethical, and continually improving
subcategory_outcome: Top management owns cyber risk, not just the CISO.
implementation_guidance: CEO/board reviews cyber risk on a regular cadence. Tone-from-the-top in town halls and policies. Cyber expectations in executive performance reviews. Leadership visible at cyber events (training kickoffs, tabletop exercises).
evidence_artifacts: Board cyber-review minutes, town-hall recordings, executive scorecards including cyber metrics.

subcategory_title: Roles, responsibilities, and authorities related to cybersecurity risk management are established, communicated, understood, and enforced
subcategory_outcome: Everyone knows their cyber responsibilities.
implementation_guidance: Maintain a RACI matrix for cyber tasks. Document roles in job descriptions. Test understanding via interviews during audits. Enforce via accountability mechanisms (annual attestations, performance reviews).
evidence_artifacts: Cyber RACI matrix, role-specific training records, annual attestation responses.

subcategory_title: Adequate resources are allocated commensurate with cybersecurity risk strategy, roles, responsibilities, and policies
subcategory_outcome: Cybersecurity is funded to match its declared importance.
implementation_guidance: Cyber budget covers headcount, tools, training, audits, and contingency. Track resourcing gaps as risks. Justify budget asks via risk-reduction analysis. Cross-charge business units that drive cyber demand.
evidence_artifacts: Cyber budget document, resourcing-gap risks in the register, business-unit cross-charge records.

subcategory_title: Cybersecurity is included in human resources practices
subcategory_outcome: Cyber considerations are baked into HR processes from hire to exit.
implementation_guidance: Background checks for sensitive roles. Cyber clauses in employment contracts. Onboarding security awareness within 30 days. Role changes trigger access reviews. Departures trigger same-day deprovisioning. Annual training mandatory.
evidence_artifacts: HR-security joint procedures, background-check records, deprovisioning logs.

subcategory_title: Policy for managing cybersecurity risks is established based on organizational context, cybersecurity strategy, and priorities and is communicated and enforced
subcategory_outcome: A cyber risk management policy exists, is communicated, and has teeth.
implementation_guidance: Develop a master cybersecurity policy covering the organization's risk approach, governance, accountabilities, and high-level controls. Approve at the highest level. Publish to all staff. Include enforcement provisions (consequences for breach). Review at least annually.
evidence_artifacts: Master cybersecurity policy, distribution acknowledgment records, annual review minutes.

subcategory_title: Policy for managing cybersecurity risks is reviewed, updated, communicated, and enforced to reflect changes in requirements, threats, technology, and organizational mission
subcategory_outcome: Policy stays current with the world it operates in.
implementation_guidance: Define a policy refresh cycle (typically annual). Trigger ad-hoc updates for major regulatory changes, breaches, technology shifts. Communicate every update via formal channels. Track acknowledgments.
evidence_artifacts: Policy version history, change-driven update records, acknowledgment tracking.

subcategory_title: Cybersecurity risk management strategy outcomes are reviewed to inform and adjust strategy and direction
subcategory_outcome: The strategy is checked for results, not just adherence.
implementation_guidance: Quarterly strategy review at executive level: are stated outcomes (e.g. 'reduce critical findings by 30%') being achieved? If not, why? Adjust strategy based on data, not just opinion.
evidence_artifacts: Strategy review minutes, outcome metrics dashboard, strategy adjustment records.

subcategory_title: The cybersecurity risk management strategy is reviewed and adjusted to ensure coverage of organizational requirements and risks
subcategory_outcome: Strategy adapts to new requirements and emerging risks.
implementation_guidance: When a new regulation, business unit, or threat type emerges, run a coverage check: does the current strategy address it? Update the strategy and resourcing accordingly. Document the trigger and the change.
evidence_artifacts: Strategy coverage review records, change-trigger log.

subcategory_title: Organizational cybersecurity risk management performance is evaluated and reviewed for adjustments needed
subcategory_outcome: Program performance is measured and managed.
implementation_guidance: Define KPIs/KRIs that measure cyber program performance (control coverage %, MTTR, training completion, audit findings trend). Report quarterly. Trigger investigation when metrics breach thresholds.
evidence_artifacts: Cyber KPI dashboard, quarterly performance reports, threshold-breach investigation records.

subcategory_title: A cybersecurity supply chain risk management program, strategy, objectives, policies, and processes are established and agreed to by organizational stakeholders
subcategory_outcome: Supply chain cyber risk has its own program, not just a contract clause.
implementation_guidance: Build a documented C-SCRM program covering supplier identification, due-diligence, contracting, monitoring, and offboarding. Get executive endorsement. Publish to procurement and security teams.
evidence_artifacts: C-SCRM program document, executive sign-off, training records.

subcategory_title: Cybersecurity roles and responsibilities for suppliers, customers, and partners are established, communicated, and coordinated internally and externally
subcategory_outcome: Everyone in the supply chain knows their cyber responsibilities.
implementation_guidance: Document RACI for the supply chain: who owns vendor risk, who reviews assessments, who approves exceptions. Include external counterparts (supplier security contacts, customer security teams).
evidence_artifacts: Supply chain cyber RACI, vendor security contact list.

subcategory_title: Cybersecurity supply chain risk management is integrated into cybersecurity and enterprise risk management, risk assessment, and improvement processes
subcategory_outcome: Supply chain risks are part of enterprise risk, not a sidebar.
implementation_guidance: Supply-chain risks live in the same register as other enterprise risks. Vendor risks roll up into enterprise dashboards. Improvements (e.g. better assessment process) tie to enterprise improvement targets.
evidence_artifacts: Enterprise risk register including supply-chain entries, integrated dashboards.

subcategory_title: Suppliers are known and prioritized by criticality
subcategory_outcome: All suppliers are inventoried and tiered.
implementation_guidance: Maintain a supplier register listing every third party with system access or that processes regulated data. Tier by criticality (Critical / High / Medium / Low) using a documented rubric. Refresh tiering annually.
evidence_artifacts: Supplier register, tiering rubric, annual review records.

subcategory_title: Requirements to address cybersecurity risks in supply chains are established, prioritized, and integrated into contracts and other types of agreements with suppliers and other relevant third parties
subcategory_outcome: Cyber requirements appear in contracts, not just policy.
implementation_guidance: Develop a standard cyber clause set sized by tier. Embed in master service agreements, DPAs (Art-28 GDPR style), and SOWs. Negotiate audit rights, breach notification windows, sub-processor approval rights.
evidence_artifacts: Standard cyber clauses by tier, signed contracts containing them.

subcategory_title: Planning and due diligence are performed to reduce risks before entering into formal supplier or other third-party relationships
subcategory_outcome: Risk is assessed before contract signing, not after.
implementation_guidance: Vendor onboarding gate: security questionnaire, evidence review (SOC 2, ISO certs, pen-test summary), risk acceptance for residual issues. Block onboarding if critical issues unresolved.
evidence_artifacts: Vendor onboarding checklist, completed questionnaires, risk-acceptance records.

subcategory_title: The risks posed by a supplier, their products and services, and other third parties are understood, recorded, prioritized, assessed, responded to, and monitored over the course of the relationship
subcategory_outcome: Vendor risks are tracked across the lifecycle, not just at onboarding.
implementation_guidance: Annual reassessment for Critical/High vendors. Continuous monitoring for cyber-relevant news (breach, ownership change, sanction). Track vendor-specific risks in the register. Escalate degradation in posture.
evidence_artifacts: Annual reassessment records, monitoring service alerts, vendor-risk register.

subcategory_title: Relevant suppliers and other third parties are included in incident planning, response, and recovery activities
subcategory_outcome: Vendors are part of your incident plan, not strangers when you call them at 3am.
implementation_guidance: Critical vendors have known on-call contacts. Joint incident drills annually with top vendors. Predefined communication channels (encrypted email, secure phone). Contracts oblige cooperation in incident response.
evidence_artifacts: Vendor incident contact roster, joint drill records, contractual cooperation clauses.

subcategory_title: Supply chain security practices are integrated into cybersecurity and enterprise risk management programs, and their performance is monitored throughout the technology product and service life cycle
subcategory_outcome: Supply chain security is monitored, not assumed.
implementation_guidance: Track supply chain KPIs: % of vendors assessed, % with current contracts, mean time to vendor breach disclosure, vendor-driven incident count. Report alongside other cyber metrics.
evidence_artifacts: Supply chain KPI dashboard, integrated cyber reporting.

subcategory_title: Cybersecurity supply chain risk management plans include provisions for activities that occur after the conclusion of a partnership or service agreement
subcategory_outcome: Vendor offboarding is handled with the same care as onboarding.
implementation_guidance: Standard offboarding checklist: data return / certified destruction, access revocation across all systems, residual obligations (warranty, support, audit cooperation), transition planning to replacement vendor.
evidence_artifacts: Offboarding checklist, signed data-destruction certificates, transition plans.

subcategory_title: Inventories of hardware managed by the organization are maintained
subcategory_outcome: Every device the organization owns or operates is inventoried.
implementation_guidance: Automated discovery feeding a central CMDB. Manual reconciliation for non-discoverable assets (lab gear, OT). Owner assigned per asset. Lifecycle states tracked (in stock, deployed, retired, destroyed). Quarterly reconciliation.
evidence_artifacts: Hardware inventory export, CMDB reconciliation reports, sample asset records showing owners.

subcategory_title: Inventories of software, services, and systems managed by the organization are maintained
subcategory_outcome: Every software product, service, and system is inventoried.
implementation_guidance: Software asset management tool tracks installs and licenses. SaaS register tracks cloud services. System catalog tracks application/system relationships. Reconcile monthly.
evidence_artifacts: Software inventory, SaaS register, system catalog, reconciliation reports.

subcategory_title: Representations of the organization's authorized network communication and internal and external network data flows are maintained
subcategory_outcome: Network architecture and data flows are documented and current.
implementation_guidance: Network diagrams with VLANs, firewalls, DMZs. Data flow diagrams for sensitive data (PII, financial, IP). Update on every architecture change. Distinct internal vs external flow views.
evidence_artifacts: Network architecture diagrams, data flow diagrams, change-driven update log.

subcategory_title: Inventories of services provided by suppliers are maintained
subcategory_outcome: Vendor-provided services are inventoried alongside owned assets.
implementation_guidance: Track every supplier-provided service: cloud, SaaS, managed services, outsourced functions. Link to the supplier register. Capture data sensitivity and criticality.
evidence_artifacts: Supplier service register, sensitivity-criticality tagging, supplier-register linkage.

subcategory_title: Assets are prioritized based on classification, criticality, resources, and impact on the mission
subcategory_outcome: Asset criticality drives control rigor.
implementation_guidance: Classify assets by data sensitivity AND business criticality (a development server may have low data sensitivity but high criticality if it deploys production). Apply controls proportionate to the higher of the two ratings.
evidence_artifacts: Asset classification rubric, classification entries on each asset, control-mapping showing rigor scaling.

subcategory_title: Inventories of data and corresponding metadata for designated data types are maintained
subcategory_outcome: Data inventory exists per data type with owners and lifecycles.
implementation_guidance: Inventory data sets that matter: customer PII, financial records, IP, regulated content. Capture metadata: owner, lawful basis (for GDPR/PDPL), retention period, location. Update on every new data flow.
evidence_artifacts: Data inventory, RoPA records, retention schedules.

subcategory_title: Systems, hardware, software, services, and data are managed throughout their life cycles
subcategory_outcome: Lifecycle management is documented and enforced.
implementation_guidance: Defined stages: plan, acquire, deploy, operate, dispose. Gate criteria at each transition (security review at acquire, hardening at deploy, decommissioning at dispose with data destruction). Track lifecycle state per asset.
evidence_artifacts: Lifecycle policy, gate review records, decommissioning certificates.

subcategory_title: Vulnerabilities in assets are identified, validated, and recorded
subcategory_outcome: Continuous identification and recording of vulnerabilities.
implementation_guidance: Schedule vulnerability scans (weekly for internet-facing, monthly internal). Validate findings (eliminate false positives). Record in vulnerability register with CVSS, exploitability, asset, owner, target remediation date.
evidence_artifacts: Vulnerability register, scan reports, validation records.

subcategory_title: Cyber threat intelligence is received from information sharing forums and sources
subcategory_outcome: Threat intel from external sources flows into the program.
implementation_guidance: Subscribe to relevant ISACs, vendor feeds, government advisories (NCA threat advisories for KSA). Triage incoming intel — does it apply to our environment? Operationalize relevant items into detections, blocks, awareness.
evidence_artifacts: Threat-intel subscription list, triage records, operationalization examples.

subcategory_title: Internal and external threats to the organization are identified and recorded
subcategory_outcome: Threat catalog is current.
implementation_guidance: Maintain a threat catalog covering internal threats (insider, error) and external (criminal, nation-state, hacktivist). Link threats to applicable assets and controls. Refresh after major events.
evidence_artifacts: Threat catalog, threat-asset-control mapping, refresh log.

subcategory_title: Potential impacts and likelihoods of threats exploiting vulnerabilities are identified and recorded
subcategory_outcome: Risk = threat × vulnerability × impact, computed per recorded combination.
implementation_guidance: For each threat-asset-vulnerability combination, score likelihood and impact using the documented methodology. Capture residual risk (after controls). Use as input to treatment decisions.
evidence_artifacts: Risk register entries with computed scores, scoring methodology, residual risk notes.

subcategory_title: Threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods, and impacts are used to understand inherent risk and inform risk response prioritization
subcategory_outcome: Risks are prioritized using rigorous data.
implementation_guidance: Sort risks by computed severity, weighting by appetite-breach status. Present to risk forum in priority order. Treatment plans address top risks first. Track remediation velocity.
evidence_artifacts: Prioritized risk register, treatment-plan ordering, velocity tracking.

subcategory_title: Risk responses are chosen, prioritized, planned, tracked, and communicated
subcategory_outcome: Every risk has a chosen response with a plan.
implementation_guidance: Each risk gets a response: Mitigate / Transfer / Avoid / Accept. Mitigations have action plans, owners, target dates. Acceptance has formal approval. Communications go to risk owner + executive sponsor.
evidence_artifacts: Risk register with response decisions, action plans, acceptance approval records.

subcategory_title: Changes and exceptions are managed, assessed for risk impact, recorded, and tracked
subcategory_outcome: Changes and exceptions don't bypass risk discipline.
implementation_guidance: Change-management process includes cyber-risk review for sensitive changes. Exceptions require documented business justification, compensating controls, expiration date, and approval at appropriate level (severity-tiered).
evidence_artifacts: Change records with cyber risk review, exception register, expiration tracking.

subcategory_title: Processes for receiving, analyzing, and responding to vulnerability disclosures are established
subcategory_outcome: External vulnerability disclosures are handled, not ignored.
implementation_guidance: Publish a security.txt file or disclosure URL. Monitor reporters@yourdomain. Triage process with SLAs (acknowledge, investigate, fix). Coordinate disclosure with reporter. Bug-bounty program for mature programs.
evidence_artifacts: Disclosure policy, security.txt, triage records, bug-bounty program (if any).

subcategory_title: The authenticity and integrity of hardware and software are assessed prior to acquisition and use
subcategory_outcome: Counterfeit and tampered hardware/software are detected before deployment.
implementation_guidance: Acquire from authorized channels. Verify signatures and hashes for software. Inspect tamper-evident seals on hardware. Maintain chain of custody. Catch suspicious packaging or branding.
evidence_artifacts: Acquisition policy, signature/hash verification records, tamper-inspection records.

subcategory_title: Critical suppliers are assessed prior to acquisition
subcategory_outcome: Pre-acquisition supplier risk review is mandatory.
implementation_guidance: Supplier risk assessment as a gate before contract signing. Cover financial stability, security maturity, geographic concentration, regulatory standing. Block acquisition until issues resolved or risk-accepted.
evidence_artifacts: Pre-acquisition assessment template, completed assessments, gate-decision records.

subcategory_title: Improvements are identified from evaluations
subcategory_outcome: Self-assessment identifies improvement opportunities.
implementation_guidance: Schedule periodic self-assessments (semi-annual recommended). Use a maturity model. Identify gaps and improvements. Build into next-cycle program plan.
evidence_artifacts: Self-assessment results, maturity scorecards, improvement plan.

subcategory_title: Improvements are identified from security tests and exercises, including those done in coordination with suppliers and relevant third parties
subcategory_outcome: Tests and exercises drive concrete improvements.
implementation_guidance: After every pen test, tabletop, red team, or DR drill, hold a post-mortem. Capture findings with owners and dates. Track to closure. Include suppliers in joint exercises.
evidence_artifacts: Test/exercise reports, post-mortem records, improvement-tracking log.

subcategory_title: Improvements are identified from execution of operational processes, procedures, and activities
subcategory_outcome: Day-to-day operations surface improvement ideas.
implementation_guidance: Encourage staff to log friction points and inefficiencies. Quarterly process reviews. Suggestion box culture. Don't punish messengers — reward improvement ideas.
evidence_artifacts: Process review minutes, suggestion log, improvement implementation tracking.

subcategory_title: Incident response plans and other cybersecurity plans that affect operations are established, communicated, maintained, and improved
subcategory_outcome: Plans are living documents, not shelfware.
implementation_guidance: Annual full review of incident response, business continuity, disaster recovery plans. Update after every real incident or exercise. Communicate updates to all affected staff. Track plan-version distribution.
evidence_artifacts: Plan version histories, post-incident updates, distribution records.

category_label: Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control
subcategory_title: Identities and credentials for authorized users, services, and hardware are managed by the organization
subcategory_outcome: Identity lifecycle is owned and managed.
implementation_guidance: Central identity provider (Azure AD, Okta, etc.). Joiner-mover-leaver process linked to HR. Service accounts in a segregated namespace with documented owners. Credential vaulting for non-human identities.
evidence_artifacts: IDP configuration, joiner-mover-leaver procedure, service-account inventory.

category_label: Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control
subcategory_title: Identities are proofed and bound to credentials based on the context of interactions
subcategory_outcome: Identity assurance matches the risk of the interaction.
implementation_guidance: Identity proofing for new users via documented method (HR-mediated for employees, business-verified for contractors, KYC for customers). Stronger proofing for elevated-access roles. Credential strength matches assurance level.
evidence_artifacts: Identity-proofing procedure, role-based assurance matrix.

category_label: Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control
subcategory_title: Users, services, and hardware are authenticated
subcategory_outcome: Every authenticated session uses verified credentials.
implementation_guidance: MFA for all users, mandatory for admins. Strong machine-to-machine auth (mTLS, signed tokens). Hardware authentication (TPM, secure enclave) where available. No shared accounts.
evidence_artifacts: MFA enrollment metrics, machine auth configurations, no-shared-account policy and audit.

category_label: Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control
subcategory_title: Identity assertions are protected, conveyed, and verified
subcategory_outcome: Identity tokens are protected end-to-end.
implementation_guidance: Short-lived tokens. Signed and encrypted assertions. Replay prevention. Token revocation mechanisms. Audit log of token issuance and use.
evidence_artifacts: Token configuration, revocation procedure, audit logs.

category_label: Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control
subcategory_title: Access permissions, entitlements, and authorizations are defined in a policy, managed, enforced, and reviewed, and incorporate the principles of least privilege and separation of duties
subcategory_outcome: Access is least-privilege and reviewed.
implementation_guidance: Role-based access control with documented permissions per role. Separation of duties for sensitive functions (e.g. requestor vs approver). Quarterly access reviews. Emergency access via break-glass with full audit.
evidence_artifacts: RBAC policy, role definitions, quarterly review records, break-glass logs.

category_label: Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control
subcategory_title: Physical access to assets is managed, monitored, and enforced commensurate with risk
subcategory_outcome: Physical access matches digital access in rigor.
implementation_guidance: Badge access to facilities. Tiered access (general office, server room, vault). Visitor escort policy. Camera coverage at sensitive points. Access logs reviewed for anomalies.
evidence_artifacts: Badge access policy, tier maps, visitor logs, camera coverage map, log review records.

subcategory_title: Personnel are provided with awareness and training so they possess the knowledge and skills to perform general tasks with cybersecurity risks in mind
subcategory_outcome: Every employee gets cyber awareness training.
implementation_guidance: Annual mandatory training for all staff. Topics: phishing, password hygiene, data handling, incident reporting. Quarterly micro-content (newsletters, short videos). Track completion. Reinforce with phishing simulations.
evidence_artifacts: Training curriculum, completion metrics, phishing simulation results.

subcategory_title: Individuals in specialized roles are provided with awareness and training so they possess the knowledge and skills to perform relevant tasks with cybersecurity risks in mind
subcategory_outcome: Specialized roles get role-specific training.
implementation_guidance: Developers train on secure coding. Admins train on hardening. IR team trains on forensics. Procurement trains on vendor security. Track role-specific training as part of competency management.
evidence_artifacts: Role-based training matrix, completion records, competency reviews.

subcategory_title: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-at-rest are protected
subcategory_outcome: Stored data is encrypted, integrity-verified, and available.
implementation_guidance: Encrypt data at rest using strong algorithms (AES-256). Use database-level encryption for sensitive tables. Hash-verify critical data. Replicate for availability. Test recovery regularly.
evidence_artifacts: Encryption-at-rest configuration, replication topology, recovery test records.

subcategory_title: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-in-transit are protected
subcategory_outcome: Data on the wire is encrypted and integrity-protected.
implementation_guidance: TLS 1.2+ for all external traffic, TLS 1.3 preferred. Certificate pinning for mobile apps. mTLS for service-to-service. No legacy protocols (SSLv3, early TLS, plain HTTP for sensitive paths). Periodic config audits.
evidence_artifacts: TLS configuration baselines, audit reports, deprecated-protocol decommissioning records.

subcategory_title: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-in-use are protected
subcategory_outcome: Data being processed in memory and applications is protected.
implementation_guidance: Memory protections (ASLR, DEP, secure enclaves). Confidential computing for very sensitive workloads. Application-level access control during processing. Audit logging of data access events.
evidence_artifacts: Memory protection configuration, confidential-computing usage records, application access logs.

subcategory_title: Backups of data are created, protected, maintained, and tested
subcategory_outcome: Backups exist, are protected, and are restorable.
implementation_guidance: 3-2-1 backup strategy (3 copies, 2 media types, 1 offsite). Backup encryption. Immutable/air-gapped copies for ransomware resilience. Quarterly restore tests. RTO/RPO documented per data class.
evidence_artifacts: Backup policy, immutability configuration, restore test records, RTO/RPO documentation.

subcategory_title: Configuration management practices are established and applied
subcategory_outcome: Configurations are managed, baselined, and drift-monitored.
implementation_guidance: Config management tool (Ansible, Puppet, Terraform). Baseline configurations per asset class. Drift detection (compare current vs baseline). Auto-remediate or alert on drift. Track baseline versions.
evidence_artifacts: Config-as-code repos, baseline definitions, drift reports.

subcategory_title: Software is maintained, replaced, and removed commensurate with risk
subcategory_outcome: Software lifecycle is risk-driven, not 'install and forget'.
implementation_guidance: Patch management with risk-based priorities (critical CVEs first). Replace EOL software. Remove unused software. Track MTTR for patching by severity.
evidence_artifacts: Patch policy, EOL replacement schedule, MTTR metrics.

subcategory_title: Hardware is maintained, replaced, and removed commensurate with risk
subcategory_outcome: Hardware lifecycle is risk-driven and secure-by-default.
implementation_guidance: Hardware replacement schedule for EOL. Secure decommissioning (data destruction certified). Maintenance contracts with vetted vendors. Spare-parts security (not from gray market).
evidence_artifacts: Hardware lifecycle policy, decommissioning certificates, maintenance contracts.

subcategory_title: Log records are generated and made available for continuous monitoring
subcategory_outcome: Critical logs flow to SIEM in real time.
implementation_guidance: Identify critical log sources (auth, network, app, cloud). Forward to SIEM via standardized format. Retain per regulation. Protect logs from tampering. Monitor log-source health.
evidence_artifacts: Log source inventory, SIEM ingestion config, retention schedule, log-health dashboard.

subcategory_title: Installation and execution of unauthorized software are prevented
subcategory_outcome: Only authorized software runs on managed endpoints.
implementation_guidance: Application allow-listing (Microsoft AppLocker, third-party). EDR with policy enforcement. Privilege restriction (no local admin for users). Periodic audit of installed software. Block unauthorized USB.
evidence_artifacts: Allow-list policy, EDR config, USB-block evidence, audit results.

subcategory_title: Secure software development practices are integrated, and their performance is monitored throughout the software development life cycle
subcategory_outcome: Security is built into the SDLC.
implementation_guidance: Security requirements in design, threat modeling for sensitive features, SAST/DAST/SCA in CI, code review with security focus, pen test before major releases, security champions in dev teams. Track DevSecOps metrics.
evidence_artifacts: SDLC security gates, threat models, SAST/DAST findings, pen test reports, DevSecOps KPIs.

subcategory_title: Networks and environments are protected from unauthorized logical access and usage
subcategory_outcome: Network access is controlled.
implementation_guidance: Network segmentation by trust zone. Firewall rules with default-deny. Zero-trust architecture progressing. Inter-zone access requires explicit allow + monitoring. Network admission control.
evidence_artifacts: Network segmentation diagram, firewall rule base, NAC configuration.

subcategory_title: The organization's technology assets are protected from environmental threats
subcategory_outcome: Physical environment threats are mitigated.
implementation_guidance: Data center selection includes environmental risk assessment (flood, earthquake, fire). Climate control. Fire suppression. UPS and generators with regular testing. Geographically diverse DR sites.
evidence_artifacts: Environmental risk assessment, DC infrastructure docs, generator test records.

subcategory_title: Mechanisms are implemented to achieve resilience requirements in normal and adverse situations
subcategory_outcome: Systems stay up under stress.
implementation_guidance: Redundancy at every tier (network paths, power, compute). Load balancing. Graceful degradation modes. Capacity planning with stress testing. Chaos engineering for mature programs.
evidence_artifacts: Architecture redundancy diagrams, capacity plans, chaos engineering reports.

subcategory_title: Adequate resource capacity to ensure availability is maintained
subcategory_outcome: Capacity is forecast and provisioned ahead of need.
implementation_guidance: Monitor utilization (CPU, memory, storage, bandwidth). Threshold-based alerts. Quarterly capacity reviews. Forward forecasting based on growth. Cloud auto-scale where applicable.
evidence_artifacts: Capacity dashboards, threshold alerts, capacity review minutes, scaling configurations.

subcategory_title: Networks and network services are monitored to find potentially adverse events
subcategory_outcome: Network behavior is monitored for anomalies.
implementation_guidance: Network monitoring tools (NDR, IDS/IPS). Baseline normal traffic. Detect deviations: unusual destinations, exfil patterns, beaconing. Tune to reduce noise. Integrate alerts with SIEM and SOC.
evidence_artifacts: NDR configuration, baseline definitions, sample alert investigations.

subcategory_title: The physical environment is monitored to find potentially adverse events
subcategory_outcome: Physical environment is continuously watched.
implementation_guidance: CCTV at sensitive entry points and inside critical rooms. Door-open sensors. Environmental sensors (smoke, water, temp, humidity). Alerts to security ops. Footage retention per policy.
evidence_artifacts: CCTV layout, sensor inventory, alert routing config, retention policy.

subcategory_title: Personnel activity and technology usage are monitored to find potentially adverse events
subcategory_outcome: Insider risk indicators are detected.
implementation_guidance: Privileged user monitoring (elevated session recording). DLP for data exfil patterns. Behavioral analytics (UEBA) for anomalous user actions. Privacy-balanced — clear policies, communicated to staff.
evidence_artifacts: PUM configuration, DLP policy, UEBA outputs, monitoring transparency policy.

subcategory_title: External service provider activities and services are monitored to find potentially adverse events
subcategory_outcome: Vendor activity in the environment is logged and reviewed.
implementation_guidance: Vendor access via dedicated accounts, time-limited, MFA-required. Log all vendor sessions. Review vendor activity periodically. Alert on after-hours or anomalous vendor activity.
evidence_artifacts: Vendor access policy, session logs, periodic review records.

subcategory_title: Computing hardware and software, runtime environments, and their data are monitored to find potentially adverse events
subcategory_outcome: Endpoints, workloads, and data behaviors are monitored.
implementation_guidance: EDR on endpoints. Workload protection (CWPP) on cloud and on-prem servers. Data activity monitoring (DAM) for databases. Centralized alerting. Tune over time.
evidence_artifacts: EDR coverage report, CWPP config, DAM logs, alert tuning history.

subcategory_title: Potentially adverse events are analyzed to better understand associated activities
subcategory_outcome: Alert triage moves from raw signal to characterized event.
implementation_guidance: Tier-1 SOC analysts triage. Enrich alerts with context (user, asset, threat intel). Determine: false positive, real event, needs investigation. Escalate to Tier-2 for sustained adverse activity.
evidence_artifacts: Triage runbooks, ticketing data, escalation records.

subcategory_title: Information is correlated from multiple sources
subcategory_outcome: Cross-source correlation enriches detections.
implementation_guidance: SIEM correlation rules across log sources. Threat intel integration to flag known-bad. UEBA for behavioral chains. Don't rely on single-source alerts for high-impact decisions.
evidence_artifacts: Correlation rule library, threat-intel feeds, UEBA correlation outputs.

subcategory_title: The estimated impact and scope of adverse events are understood
subcategory_outcome: Impact assessment for each event before response is sized.
implementation_guidance: Define impact assessment criteria: data classes affected, systems impacted, users involved, regulatory implications, business processes disrupted. Apply consistently in triage. Drive response severity.
evidence_artifacts: Impact assessment template, sample assessments, severity-tier definitions.

subcategory_title: Information on adverse events is provided to authorized staff and tools
subcategory_outcome: Right people get right info at right time.
implementation_guidance: Defined notification chains by severity. Automated routing in SIEM. On-call rotations. Status pages for stakeholders during incidents. Post-incident communications to affected parties.
evidence_artifacts: Notification chain doc, SIEM routing config, on-call schedules.

subcategory_title: Cyber threat intelligence and other contextual information are integrated into the analysis
subcategory_outcome: Context elevates raw alerts into informed conclusions.
implementation_guidance: Threat intel feeds integrated into SIEM/SOAR. IOC matching against alerts. Threat actor TTPs (MITRE ATT&CK) for hunt and detection. Vulnerability context (is this asset patched?).
evidence_artifacts: Intel-feed integration, IOC match logs, MITRE-mapped detections.

subcategory_title: Incidents are declared when adverse events meet the defined incident criteria
subcategory_outcome: Crossing the criteria triggers the formal IR machinery.
implementation_guidance: Documented incident-declaration criteria (severity, scope, impact). Authority to declare clearly assigned. Trigger automation: ticket, war room, comms, IR team mobilization.
evidence_artifacts: Incident criteria document, declaration authority matrix, recent declaration records.

subcategory_title: The incident response plan is executed in coordination with relevant third parties once an incident is declared
subcategory_outcome: When the bell rings, the plan runs.
implementation_guidance: On declaration, trigger IR plan: war-room established, IR lead assigned, comms tree opened, vendors/partners notified. Execute predefined response playbooks. Document every action.
evidence_artifacts: IR plan, recent incident records, war-room logs.

subcategory_title: Incident reports are triaged and validated
subcategory_outcome: Reported incidents are quickly assessed for accuracy and severity.
implementation_guidance: Tier-1 validates reports (real or false alarm). Tier-2 sizes severity. Escalate to IR lead. Track validation time as KPI. Reduce mean time to validate via runbooks.
evidence_artifacts: Validation runbooks, triage records, MTV KPI.

subcategory_title: Incidents are categorized and prioritized
subcategory_outcome: Categorization drives response.
implementation_guidance: Categories: data breach, ransomware, insider, DDoS, supply-chain, etc. Priority by impact + urgency. Re-categorize as facts evolve. Categories drive playbook selection.
evidence_artifacts: Categorization scheme, priority matrix, playbook selection logic.

subcategory_title: Incidents are escalated or elevated as needed
subcategory_outcome: Right people involved at right time.
implementation_guidance: Escalation criteria documented (severity rises, scope expands, regulator notification needed, executive comms required). Automated triggers in IR tooling. Tested via tabletops.
evidence_artifacts: Escalation matrix, ticketing-tool config, tabletop records.

subcategory_title: Incident response criteria are applied to determine which incidents have been resolved and to inform additional response activities
subcategory_outcome: Closure is data-driven, not assumed.
implementation_guidance: Resolution criteria: containment confirmed, eradication verified, recovery validated, lessons logged. Independent verification before closure. Trigger lessons-learned process.
evidence_artifacts: Resolution criteria, closure records, lessons-learned reports.

subcategory_title: Analysis is performed to establish what has taken place during an incident and the root cause of the incident
subcategory_outcome: Root cause is found, not papered over.
implementation_guidance: Forensic analysis for sustained or sensitive incidents. Timeline reconstruction. Root cause analysis (5-whys, fishbone). Document findings. Address root cause, not just symptoms.
evidence_artifacts: Forensic reports, timelines, RCA documents.

subcategory_title: Actions performed during an investigation are recorded, and the records' integrity and provenance are preserved
subcategory_outcome: Evidence chain is preserved for legal/forensic use.
implementation_guidance: Investigation log with timestamps and actor IDs. Forensic image capture before changes. Hash verification. Chain of custody for physical evidence. Designated evidence custodian.
evidence_artifacts: Investigation logs, forensic images with hashes, chain-of-custody forms.

subcategory_title: Incident data and metadata are collected, and their integrity and provenance are preserved
subcategory_outcome: Incident artifacts are reliably retained.
implementation_guidance: Centralized incident-evidence repository. Immutable storage. Defined retention by incident category and regulatory requirements. Restrict access.
evidence_artifacts: Evidence repository, immutability config, retention policy, access logs.

subcategory_title: An incident's magnitude is estimated and validated
subcategory_outcome: Incident size is quantified, not guessed.
implementation_guidance: Estimate impact: records affected, dollar value, system downtime, customer count. Validate via independent verification (e.g. database count vs sample audit). Update estimates as facts develop.
evidence_artifacts: Magnitude estimates with validation, update history.

subcategory_title: Internal and external stakeholders are notified of incidents
subcategory_outcome: Stakeholder communication is timely and accurate.
implementation_guidance: Predefined comm matrix: who tells whom, when, what. Internal stakeholders (exec, legal, comms, HR). External (customers, regulators, law enforcement). Templates for common scenarios. Legal and PR review for external comms.
evidence_artifacts: Communication matrix, templates, recent incident comms.

subcategory_title: Information is shared with designated internal and external stakeholders
subcategory_outcome: Information sharing reaches the right audiences with the right detail.
implementation_guidance: Tiered comms: detailed for IR team, summarized for execs, customer-friendly for affected parties. Avoid leaks. Track who received what when. Coordinate with legal counsel.
evidence_artifacts: Comms tracking, distribution records, legal review records.

subcategory_title: Incidents are contained
subcategory_outcome: Containment limits damage spread.
implementation_guidance: Immediate containment: isolate affected systems, block malicious IPs, reset credentials, disable compromised accounts. Short-term containment if longer-term fix needed. Document containment rationale.
evidence_artifacts: Containment runbooks, recent containment actions, post-incident reports.

subcategory_title: Incidents are eradicated
subcategory_outcome: Threat is removed from the environment.
implementation_guidance: Identify and remove all malicious artifacts (malware, persistence, backdoors). Patch exploited vulnerability. Re-image if uncertain. Hunt for related compromises elsewhere.
evidence_artifacts: Eradication runbooks, IOC sweeps, re-imaging records, hunt results.

subcategory_title: The recovery portion of the incident response plan is executed once initiated from the incident response process
subcategory_outcome: Recovery follows the plan, not improvisation.
implementation_guidance: Recovery plan triggered after eradication. Defined RTO/RPO targets. Restore from clean backups. Validate integrity before returning to service. Coordinate cutover with business.
evidence_artifacts: Recovery plan, recovery records, RTO/RPO compliance reports.

subcategory_title: Recovery actions are selected, scoped, prioritized, and performed
subcategory_outcome: Recovery is sequenced for maximum business value.
implementation_guidance: Prioritize recovery by business criticality. Critical systems first, dependents next. Validate each recovery before next. Provide manual workarounds for delayed systems.
evidence_artifacts: Recovery sequence, validation records, workaround documentation.

subcategory_title: The integrity of backups and other restoration assets is verified before using them for restoration
subcategory_outcome: Restored data is verified clean before deployment.
implementation_guidance: Hash-verify backups before restore. Scan for malware in restored data. Test in isolated environment. Only promote to production once verified.
evidence_artifacts: Verification logs, malware scan results, isolation-test records.

subcategory_title: Critical mission functions and cybersecurity risk management are considered to establish post-incident operational norms
subcategory_outcome: Post-incident state is sustainable, not fragile.
implementation_guidance: After recovery, review what new norms emerge: tighter monitoring, new controls, residual constraints. Bake into BAU operations. Don't let temporary measures become permanent without governance.
evidence_artifacts: Post-incident review, new-norm decisions, BAU integration records.

subcategory_title: The integrity of restored assets is verified, systems and services are restored, and normal operating status is confirmed
subcategory_outcome: Recovery is confirmed complete via objective tests.
implementation_guidance: Functional tests. Performance tests. User acceptance verification. Monitoring shows no residual indicators. Formal closure of incident only after validation.
evidence_artifacts: Test results, monitoring snapshots, formal closure records.

subcategory_title: The end of incident recovery is declared based on criteria, and incident-related documentation is completed
subcategory_outcome: Recovery has a definitive end-state.
implementation_guidance: End-of-recovery criteria documented. Final report covering full timeline, decisions, costs, lessons. Distribute to stakeholders. Archive in incident management system.
evidence_artifacts: End criteria, final report, archive records.

subcategory_title: Recovery activities and progress in restoring operational capabilities are communicated to designated internal and external stakeholders
subcategory_outcome: Recovery progress is transparent to stakeholders.
implementation_guidance: Status pages updated regularly during recovery. Customer comms at meaningful milestones. Internal updates at defined cadence. Honest about delays and obstacles. Avoid speculation.
evidence_artifacts: Status page snapshots, customer comms, internal-update logs.

subcategory_title: Public updates on incident recovery are shared using approved methods and messaging
subcategory_outcome: Public communications are coordinated and brand-safe.
implementation_guidance: PR/Comms team owns public messaging. Legal review on regulatory implications. Centralized voice (no rogue exec statements). Templates for common scenarios. Track public and media reactions.
evidence_artifacts: PR-approved templates, public statements, media tracking.
